nary_nodes.label: Soyuz MS-29/75S Crew Launch
evidence: Physician-astronaut Anil Menon, a former flight surgeon with NASA and then SpaceX who rejoined NASA as an astronaut along with his wife Anna, rocketed into space Tuesday with two Russian cosmonauts for an eight-month stay aboard the International Space Station.
Soyuz MS-29/75S commander Pyotr Dubrov, flanked on his left by cosmonaut Anna Kikina and on the right by Menon, blasted off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan at 10:47 a.m. EDT.
nary_nodes.type_definition: The event of a spacecraft or rocket being launched into space.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class adequately describes a space launch event. All candidates are unsuitable.

nary_nodes.label: Soyuz MS-29/75S Released
evidence: Eight minutes and 46 seconds later, the Soyuz was released to fly on its own, catching up with the station after just two orbits and moving in for docking at 1:52 p.m.
nary_nodes.type_definition: The event of a spacecraft being released from another vehicle or structure.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class adequately describes a spacecraft release event. All candidates are unsuitable.

nary_nodes.label: Soyuz MS-29/75S Docking
evidence: Eight minutes and 46 seconds later, the Soyuz was released to fly on its own, catching up with the station after just two orbits and moving in for docking at 1:52 p.m.
But the ship flew itself in for a picture-perfect docking at Russia's Earth-facing Prichal module as the two spacecraft sailed 260 miles above the Mediterranean Sea.
nary_nodes.type_definition: The event of two spacecraft connecting in space.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class adequately describes a spacecraft docking event. All candidates are unsuitable.

nary_nodes.label: Russians Extending ISS Visits
evidence: With a few exceptions, station flights have typically lasted for five to six months, but the Russians are now extending visits to eight months to reduce the amount of cargo that has to be shipped up.

nary_nodes.label: NASA-Roscosmos Agreement
evidence: Menon is part of the Soyuz crew under an agreement between NASA and Roscosmos, the Russian federal space agency, that calls for at least one NASA astronaut to launch aboard each Soyuz and one cosmonaut to go up aboard each SpaceX Crew Dragon.

The agreement ensures at least one American and at least one Russian are always aboard the station to operate their respective systems in case a Soyuz or Dragon has to depart early because of a medical emergency or some other major problem.

nary_nodes.label: Anna Kikina's First Space Flight
evidence: As for Kikina, who first flew to space aboard a Crew Dragon in 2022, Menon described her as "100 percent full on energy, and really adds a lot to our team because me and Pyotr are a bit more quiet, and so it's really cool to have her just like keep the engine running and moving us along.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class adequately describes a space flight event. All candidates are unsuitable.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on low chances of flying to space
evidence: "In terms of me and Anna, I would say there was a zero percent chance we thought this would happen, but it does go to show that if you keep working at something, you should never count yourself out," Anil Menon said.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on diverse paths to NASA/space
evidence: "It also goes to show that if you're interested in being a part of NASA, going to space, there's a lot of different ways this could work out.
There isn't a set course.
Sometimes... if you work hard and consistently over time, the results can be completely shocking.
We've been absolutely shocked by this."

nary_nodes.label: Isaacman's congratulations to crew
evidence: "Congratulations, crew, on a impressive three-hour (rendezvous)," he radioed from Baikonur.
"And to my friend Anil, how are you enjoying space flight?"

nary_nodes.label: Menon's reply to Isaacman
evidence: "Hello, it's great to hear from you," Menon replied.
"An incredibly fast ride!
I'm feeling great."

nary_nodes.label: Isaacman's message of pride and well wishes
evidence: "I know you all have a lot of work to do right now, so just passing on to you (that) all your friends here, your family, your nation are proud of you," Isaacman said.
"Godspeed and God bless on the expedition ahead."

nary_nodes.label: Menon's thanks for kind words
evidence: "Thank you very much for those kind words," Menon said.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's description of the ISS
evidence: "The station is a sight to behold and a monument to all the hard work we are able to do together and what we're able to achieve when we do it.

nary_nodes.label: Dubrov's statement on welcome tradition
evidence: "It's a great tradition when the arriving crew is welcomed by the smiley faces of our crewmates," Dubrov said through an interpreter.
"We passed a lot of time together during our training, and now we are here all together on the station.
And also, those traditional hugs.
It's so amazing, it's very warm and comes from the heart."

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on difficulty of staying home
evidence: In an interview with CBS News, Menon said staying at home with the kids while his wife flew in space was more difficult than he expected.
Now that their roles are reversed, both are gaining a better understanding of the challenges faced by both.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on previous stress
evidence: "When we talk about what it was like for her to launch and me to be on the ground, I think that was the harder job, and I found it really stressful," he said.
"I was worried about her and the kids, and there were certain challenges related to that.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on sharing perspective
evidence: "I'm able to share that perspective with her, so I'm like, hey, heads up, like it's going to be a lot easier for me to do this launch."

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on Anna's insight
evidence: For her part, he added, "she's got insight into what that's like (to fly in space) and what the launch might be like, and how to make it meaningful....
We've talked a lot about that.
I think, like, either side of this, my side and her side, hopefully we're better off, and we understand each other a bit better."

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on flying with space veterans
evidence: Menon said he was lucky to be flying with space veterans like Dubrov and Kikina.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's description of Pyotr Dubrov
evidence: He described his Soyuz commander as "kind of on the quieter side, really intellectual, really sharp."
"He speaks incredibly good English, and he's into Rubik's cubes and esoteric science fiction.
He's read the Foundation series (by) Isaac Asimov, and Murderbot before the TV shows made those things popular.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's statement on hitting it off with Dubrov
evidence: We really hit it off, because I love science fiction, too, and that's super cool."

nary_nodes.label: Menon's description of Anna Kikina
evidence: As for Kikina, who first flew to space aboard a Crew Dragon in 2022, Menon described her as "100 percent full on energy, and really adds a lot to our team because me and Pyotr are a bit more quiet, and so it's really cool to have her just like keep the engine running and moving us along.
"And she's an athlete, like a rafter boater, she was on the Russian version of American Gladiator -- it's called Titan -- and won that easily.

nary_nodes.label: Menon's description of the crew
evidence: And so it's a cool crew, an interesting, fun crew to be a part of as well.
They've also flown to space, so I got a lot to learn and pick up from them, and it's a good spot to be in."
